newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool prices continue rise in week.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool prices continue rise in week.

text.p: Australian wool prices maintained the momentum of previous week with further increases recorded at sales this week in Sydney, Launceston and Fremantle, the Australian Council of Wool Exporters said in its weekly report.
The eastern market indicator rose 13 cents to 621 cents a kg clean, reaching the highest level for the season. The western market indicator rose 17 cents to 599 cents a kg clean.
A total of 71,707 bales were offered, with the trade taking about 94 percent. The pass-in rate was six percent.
The council said the combination of another relatively low quantity and a continuation of the more widespread competition evident last week provided the strength in the market this week.
"The positive tone reflected by price movements in recent weeks will be most welcomed by growers seeking confidence for the future," the council said.
Wool International said its stockpile of unsold wool totalled 1,855,173 as at February 20.
In the futures market, a total of 136 contracts were traded in the 21 micron contract in the week ended February 20.
Open interest fell 35 contracts to close at 805.
The February 1997 contract closed 29 cents up at 729 cents/kg clean.
The April 1997 contract closed 12 cents up at 736 cents/kg clean.
Sales next week are in Newcastle, Melbourne and Fremantle with a total of 93,600 bales rostered for sale.
